# Query Selector All

The `document.querySelectorAll()` method finds all elements on the page that match a CSS selector. Use it when you want to select a group of elements, such as all buttons, all cards, or all elements with the same class.
examples: [{"name":"Select All Cards","description":"This selects every element with the class `card.`","code":"`const cards = document.querySelectorAll(\".card\");`"},{"name":"Select All Buttons","description":"This selects all `button` elements on the page.","code":"`const buttons = document.querySelectorAll(\"button\");`"}]
name: Query Selector All
tips:
- `document.querySelectorAll()` selects all elements that match the selector.
- Use `.` before a class name, like `".card"`.
- Use `#` before an `id`, like `"#main"`, but `id` values should usually be unique.
- Remember to put the selector inside quotation marks.
- In Web Lab, this method is often used when code needs to update or check several elements on the page.
